findings.title: Phone (390×844): TURN, LAYER, VIA, CHECK and SHIP are off-screen, so a touch player can't finish the job
findings.problem: At the bench in portrait, the bench camera only pulls back by clamp(1.25/aspect,1,2.1) (src/game.ts:372). The 3D tool pucks sit at x=±1.58 m either side of the board (src/stations/qfn/station.ts:99-106), so only UNDO (x=-1.08) is still in frame. The board itself shrinks to about 250 px wide (s5 log: cell centres span x 70–320), so a cell is about 19 px, well under a usable touch target. CHECK and SHIP have keyboard fallbacks only (C and Enter, station.ts:27). The prompt pill reads 'Enter Ship' but can't be tapped (src/ui/objectives.ts:93 adds no handler). A phone player can place parts and draw tracks, but can never ship a board, so the room can't be completed. The phone layout CSS also hides the net list (qfn.css:9), so the board's progress is invisible on a phone. Review 3 (REVIEW_A §1) already reported that 'On QFN none of MOVE, TURN, PEN, ERASE or SHIP are visible'. It is still open.
findings.fix: 1) Add an optional `viewPortrait` to the Station interface (src/stations/types.ts) and use it in src/game.ts:372 when cam.aspect<1. For QFN, `{distance:9.5,pitch:1.25,lookY:.2}` puts the board at the top of the frame. 2) In QfnBench.buildBench, when innerWidth<innerHeight, lay the five pucks out in one row under the board (z = board near edge + 0.45, x = -1.2…1.2, 0.6 m apart) instead of at the sides, and rebuild them on resize. 3) Make the prompt pill tappable: in ObjectivesHUD, a pointerdown on .prompt-pill while g.atBench calls g.station.key(code) for the shown key (Enter→ship, C→check). 4) At aspect<1, scale S (cell size) up so a cell is ≥ 36 px.
findings.verify: Retake mockups/review5/tools/qfn-play/s5-phone.mjs. All five buttons are visible in qfn-play-62. Add a Playwright spec at viewport 390×844 that taps the SHIP puck through its projected screen position (like the 'real pointer' test in tests/station-qfn.spec.ts) and expects station.board to advance.
findings.verify_reason:
Reproduced at 390×844 (verify-qfn-play-20-phone-bench.jpg). Only the UNDO puck is in frame. TURN, LAYER, VIA, CHECK and SHIP (station.ts:99-106, x=±1.58) are off-screen. The board spans x 70–320 px, about 20.8 px per cell. The prompt pill is a plain div with no handler (objectives.ts:93). qfn.css:9 hides the net list under 700 px, and the phone panel shows only the header. Touch play is supported (screens.css:240/289 virtual stick), so a touch-only player can't CHECK or SHIP and can't finish the room. P0 holds for phones. | P0 re-check confirmed: I couldn't refute it. A phone player in portrait can't ship a board, so P0 stands. Repro script: mockups/review5/tools/p0check-qfn-play/c1-phone.mjs (args: W H tag). It reaches the bench the same way tests/station-qfn.spec.ts does. It solves board 1 with the REFERENCE route (tier 3). Then it scans the whole canvas with pointermoves (the station sets cursor:pointer over a clickable puck) and taps every clickable spot with a real mouse click.

PORTRAIT 390×844 (shots p0check-qfn-play-portrait-01-bench.jpg and -02-solved-before-ship.png, both looked at):
- Board cells span x 70–320 px, about 20.8 px per cell.
- Only 2 clickable regions exist on screen: a 1-px sliver of a left puck at x=0, y 468–504 (tapping it does nothing), and UNDO at (39,537). Tapping UNDO set the solved board back to tier 0.
- Nothing on the right half of the screen is clickable, so CHECK and SHIP can't be reached.
- The pill reads 'Enter Ship'. A real tap on it at (195,734) did nothing (board 0, shipped 0). It is a plain div; src/ui/objectives.ts:93 adds no handler to it, unlike the bench chip at :96.
- At the bench the camera can't be moved. src/game.ts:372 forces yaw and pitch and applies clamp(1.25/aspect,1,2.1). The wheel listener returns early at the bench (src/game.ts:175). Touch has no right-drag orbit. So the player can't bring the pucks into view.
- Nothing else ships a board: KEYS (src/stations/qfn/station.ts:27) is keyboard only, the bench-chip only stands you up, and the station panel has no buttons.
- Result: a touch player in portrait can never ship, and the room can't be finished.

LANDSCAPE 844×390 (a possible way round it): taps do work there. A tap at (663,303) shipped board 1 (shot -03-shipped-by-tap.png). But that only works blind. The CHECK and SHIP hit area (x 624–702, y 270–336) lies entirely under the opaque station panel (x about 530–820, y 98–340; shot p0check-qfn-play-landscape-02-solved-before-ship.jpg). Taps only get through because .station-panel has pointer-events:none (src/ui/ui.css:218). The pill tap also fails in landscape. Nothing tells the player to turn the phone. So landscape is not a workaround anyone could find, and the fix should cover it too: in landscape, move the pucks or the panel so CHECK and SHIP aren't hidden under it.

Fix: I agree with the verifier's corrected fix. Their reasons are right that the original part 1 shrinks the visible width and that 36 px cells can't fit across 13 cells. The changes:
- In portrait, lay the pucks out below the board.
- Add DOM CHECK and SHIP buttons under (pointer:coarse).
- Make .prompt-pill call g.station.key(code) on pointerdown while g.atBench.
- Keep the pucks clear of the .station-panel rect in landscape.

Verify with this c1-phone.mjs at 390×844 and 844×390. The scan should find all 6 pucks inside the viewport and outside the panel rect, and a tap on the pill or SHIP should advance station.board. There were no console errors in either run.
extra_evidence: src/ui/screens.css:240 (touch stick exists, so touch is a supported platform)
findings.fix_correction: Part 1 is wrong. A shorter camera distance (9.5 against today's 5.6×2.1≈11.8) narrows the visible width, which would push the pucks further off-screen. Part 4 can't be done as written: 13 cells × 36 px = 468 px, wider than a 390 px screen. Corrected fix: in portrait, turn the bench camera 90° (yaw offset in game.ts:372 when cam.aspect<1) so the board's 9-cell side runs across the screen (9×0.15 m). Lay the 5 pucks plus UNDO out in one or two rows below the board (rebuild on resize). Also add DOM buttons for CHECK and SHIP to the bench chip under @media (pointer:coarse), and make .prompt-pill call g.station.key(code) on pointerdown while g.atBench. Verify with a 390×844 spec that taps the SHIP control and expects station.board to advance.

findings.title: Throwing the parts crate at the bench never delivers it, so the one chaos act in the room is ignored
findings.problem: The only physical job in the Fabrication Bay is carrying the crate. The obvious Good Job move is to throw it (Q) at the bench. The throw path (src/game.ts:183) applies an impulse and never calls station.dropped(). Only the E put-down path calls it (src/game.ts:210 → station.ts:378-383). In s3 the crate landed at (1.84, 0.62), 2.15 m from the stand, which is inside the 2.2 m accept radius, but partsReady stayed false. The prompt then switched to 'E Grab the bin' because the crate was out of reach. A thrown crate that sails over the bench (s7 'bench-top' case) lands behind it next to the yellow cart, where the straight walk back fails. So the chaos shortcut is silently refused, and the player has to walk over, pick it up and put it down properly, which is the 'tidy' route. AGENTS 5 asks for chaos shortcuts second, never punished. Here chaos is ignored and costs time, and the throw also adds damage (see the grading finding).
findings.fix: In QfnBench.update(): if !partsReady and the crate isn't held, its linvel < 0.4 m/s, and it lies within 2.2 m of the side table (table.x+2.55, table.z) or of the stand, run the same accept code as dropped(). Factor that code out as accept(p). If it landed by a throw (set a flag on throw in game.ts:183 for spec.id==='parts'), add a bigger burst ('confetti', 20) and a cheer, and count a new bonus 'Slam-dunk the parts crate'. Also widen the side-table catch: make the side table's top a sensor that accepts the crate on contact, so a crate that lands on the bench top or side table counts.
findings.verify: New spec in tests/station-qfn.spec.ts: walk to (-2.8,-.5) holding the crate, press Q, wait(3), expect station.partsReady===true. Retake qfn-play-42 so it shows the crate on the side table with the burst.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced. After Q from (-3.08,-0.44), the crate came to rest at (1.84, 0.32, 0.62), 2.15 m from the stand and inside the 2.2 m radius, but partsReady stayed false for 6 s. The prompt switched to 'E Grab the bin'. The throw branch in game.ts:183 never calls station.dropped(). Only the E path (game.ts:204) does, and QfnBench.update() (station.ts:384-398) never checks where the crate is. In verify-qfn-play-03 the landed crate can't be seen at all: it's hidden behind the cabinet stack.

findings.title: After the first ~5 s the 120-prop room is only a backdrop: no cable, no chaos route, no physical bonus
findings.problem: The whole room phase is spawn → crate (2.3 m, about 1 s) → bench (about 10 m, about 2 s). s2 timing: crate grabbed at t=1.0, crate on the bench at t=3.2, seated at t=5.3. After that the whole job (three boards, about 40 inputs) happens at the bench camera. There's no cable in the room: it's hidden and not simulated in station rooms (src/game.ts:92, :104), even though the level declares anchor (-10,6) and length 10 (src/levels/qfn.ts:22). All three bonuses are bench metrics (station.ts:74-77). obstacles is []. The pick-and-place, reflow oven and AOI along the back wall (room.ts:347-366) are scenery the job never touches. Shipped boards appear as flat slabs on the side table (station.ts:296-297) that nobody carries anywhere. Review 4 (DESIGN_A §2) said 'after the crate the room contributes nothing', and it is still true. It fails the cable-is-the-star rule, the chaos-route rule and the bonus-in-world rule.
findings.fix: Give each shipped board one physical leg in the room, using what is already modelled. On SHIP, the board pops out of the jig as a carryable id'd prop ('board1'…'board3', small MASK-green slab). Pip carries it to the reflow oven's in-conveyor (1.8-2.55, z -6.9) or throws it on (that's the chaos shortcut, and it always succeeds if it lands on the conveyor). The oven's windows pulse, and the board comes out by the AOI, whose screen shows a green tick. Make 'Ship' a goal: the step text becomes 'Board 2 baked'. Add a bonus 'Toss a board straight onto the oven belt'. Optional cable beat: the bench's test lead (finite 6 m) has to be dragged from a wall socket to the board's J1 for the power-on test, which gives the room a short cable with strain and slingshot.
findings.verify: Spec: after ship(), a 'board1' item exists; throw it at (1.8,-6.3) and expect the step to complete. Survey shot shows the board on the conveyor. snap().rope.maxLength>0 with a visible cable if the test-lead variant is chosen.
findings.verify_reason: Code checks out. The cable, plug, socket and anchor are hidden in station rooms (game.ts:92), and simulateCable runs only when !station (game.ts:104). Yet snap().rope.maxLength still reports 10 (verify log). All three bonuses are bench metrics (station.ts:74-77). obstacles:[] (qfn.ts:22). Shipped boards are static slabs (station.ts:296-297). The room has no physical cable act at all, which breaks DR-05 ('every playable room') and DR-10 outright.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-qfn-play/v1-room.mjs log: rope maxLength 10 while the cable is hidden
findings.fix_correction: The oven-leg idea alone doesn't meet DR-05, because DR-05 needs a cable act. The test-lead variant (finite lead with strain and slingshot from a wall socket to J1 for a power-on test) should be the required part, not optional. The oven leg covers DR-01 and DR-10.

findings.title: Room chaos and bench mistakes share a damage limit of 1 and a cost limit only 25% over track par, so one throw costs a grade
findings.problem: QfnBench.limits = {time:720, damage:1, cost:ceil(Σpar×1.25)=124} (station.ts:51, :68). At the result, game.ts:353 adds the station score (board send-backs and track cost) to the room's game.damage and game.cost. Room damage comes from any prop that hits at more than 5.5 m/s (game.ts:335), and the crate itself counts. In s8 a single crate throw at a coworker showed damage 1 and cost 5 on the HUD, then damage 2 and cost 10 on the pause screen (qfn-play-90, -91). That already exceeds limits.damage=1, so the damage axis drops to B before the player has even sat down. A clean bench run costs 99 of the 124 cost budget, so knocking over one cart (cost 50) drops the cost axis to B. 'Damage' therefore means two different things (a broken mug and a board sent back from test) on one axis tuned for the bench alone. Pure wrecking is no worse than one layout mistake. The best-of-three overall hides it, but the per-axis medals on the result card read as a telling-off for chaos.
findings.fix: Either keep the axes separate (grade room breakage with the floor's own rule and send-backs as 'mistakes'), or tune the limits for both: limits={time:720, damage:1+6, cost:ceil(par×1.25)+60}. Exclude the job item: in game.ts:335, skip the damage counter when prop.spec.id==='parts' (the crate is meant to be thrown). Show on the result card which axis earned the overall grade.
findings.verify: Rerun s8-alarm.mjs, then the clean solve. The result shows damage A after one crate throw plus a clean bench. A spec that wrecks 5 props and then solves cleanly still gets three A medals except damage B or better.
findings.verify_reason: The mechanics are right. limits={time:720,damage:1,cost:ceil(99×1.25)=124} (station.ts:51,68; pars 22+35+42 in logic.ts:78-92). Room breakage, the job crate included (game.ts:335 has no id exclusion), is added to station mistakes on one axis (game.ts:353). qfn-play-91 shows damage 2 and cost 10 after one throw, so the damage axis is B. The claimed harm is overstated, though. overall=[...parts].sort()[0] is the best axis (grade.ts:6), so the overall grade doesn't drop. DR-07 only asks that a clean run can earn A everywhere and that pure wrecking can't, and both hold. damage:1 is also the house value for garage, observatory and spectrum, so this isn't specific to QFN. It's a per-axis polish issue, not P1. My own crate throw at the bench registered no damage, so the effect depends on what the crate hits.
findings.fix_correction: Don't raise damage to 1+6. That would let 7 send-backs earn A and mix the two meanings again. Instead rank the damage axis as the worse of two separate ranks: room breakage against the cable-floor default (10) and bench send-backs against 1. Alternatively show them as two rows. Excluding prop.spec.id==='parts' from game.ts:335 is fine.

findings.title: 'E Set the crate on the bench' shows where pressing E drops the crate on the floor
findings.problem: prompt() shows 'Set the crate on the bench' whenever Pip is within 2.6 m of the stand (station.ts:424). dropped() accepts only when the crate's position, held 1.05 m ahead of Pip (game.ts:331), is within 2.2 m of the side table or the stand (station.ts:380). Facing away from or past the bench, the prompt promises one thing and E does another. s3: Pip at (-2.35, 0.54), 2.57 m from the stand, facing -z, prompt 'E Set the crate on the bench'. The crate went to (-2.67,-0.41), 2.57 m from the stand, and was dropped on the floor with partsReady=false and no feedback. A new player who trusts the prompt sees nothing happen and doesn't know why.
findings.fix: Use one predicate for both. Add `crateLands(pos)` in QfnBench that tests Pip's own position (<2.6 m from the stand, or <2.6 m from the side table) rather than the crate's, and call it from prompt() and dropped(). Since dropped() snaps the crate onto the side table anyway (station.ts:381), the crate's own position doesn't matter. Also give the 'hm' voice and a toast if E drops the crate elsewhere near the bench.
findings.verify: s3-chaos 'facing away near bench' step: after E, expect station.partsReady===true. Add a spec that approaches the stand from the -x side facing +z and drops the crate.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced exactly. Pip was at (-2.35,0.54) with the prompt 'E Set the crate on the bench'. After E the crate fell to (-2.67,0.27,-0.41), partsReady stayed false, and the prompt changed silently to 'E Grab the crate', with no toast or sound. The prompt checks Pip's distance (<2.6, station.ts:424) while dropped() checks the crate's position (<2.2, station.ts:380).

findings.title: A cabinet stack in front of the bench hides Pip at the default camera, and later the thrown crate
findings.problem: Seeded clutter puts a 'cabinets' recipe (two cabinets with a box on top at y 1.9, src/levels/clutter.ts:47) at about (0.6, 1.77). That is directly between the default orbit camera and the bench stand at (0,-0.5). Standing at the bench or walking up with the crate, Pip is hidden below the hat (qfn-play-13, -57, -70). The thrown crate in qfn-play-42 is also hidden behind it, with only the marker showing. Only pillars are occluders (src/levels/decor.ts:55), so the stack never fades. The clutter lane (src/levels/qfn.ts:25, r 1.05) keeps the walking route clear but not the camera's line of sight to the work spot. The audit also reports this cabinet and its top box interpenetrating by 0.02 (s1 audit: 'cabinet @0.6,1.77' / 'box @0.6,1.77').
findings.fix: 1) In src/levels/qfn.ts clutter, add a camera keep-clear lane from the stand toward the default camera: `{points:[[0,-.5],[0,5.5]],r:1.8}` (the same for any station level). 2) Generic fix, DR-12: in the occlusion pass (src/game.ts:386-388), fade any mesh taller than 1.2 m hit by rays to Pip's feet, chest and head, cabinets and stacked clutter included. 3) Lower the recipe's top box to sit on the cabinet top (y = cabinet height + half box) to clear the 0.02 overlap.
findings.verify: Retake qfn-play-13 and -70. Pip's body is fully visible at the stand. g.audit(.02) on qfn returns no cabinet/box pair.
findings.verify_reason: qfn-play-70 and -13 show Pip at the stand hidden behind the cabinet stack, with only the hat visible. My throw shot (verify-qfn-play-03) shows the landed crate fully hidden by the same kind of stack. Occluders are only interior walls and pillars (decor.ts:49-55), and DR-12 lists cabinets as meshes that must fade. One sub-claim is refuted: g.audit(.02) at start returns [] (no overlaps). At audit(.005) the cabinet@0.6,1.77/box pair overlaps by only 0.01, which is resting contact under DR-70's 0.02 threshold.
findings.fix_correction: Fade props per instance, not per material. toon() materials are shared by colour (render/toon.ts:33-44), so fading one cabinet's material would fade every prop of that colour. Clone the material on the occluding prop when it first fades, or use a per-object opacity uniform. Drop fix step 3 (the audit overlap isn't real). The keep-clear lane from the stand toward the camera is fine.

findings.title: Bench HUD carries about 60–80 words and says the board's name three times
findings.problem: With the board open at 1440×900, the frame shows these at once. Job card: 'Board 1 · Sensor breakout: one layer, no crossings', 8 words. Right panel: header 'BOARD 1/3 · ONE LAYER Sensor breakout', the ask sentence of 13–25 words, a 4-net legend with pad counts, then Connector, Loop, Track + vias and Grade now rows, about 30 words. The in-world plate 'BOARD 1 · SENSOR BREAKOUT' and the legend 'still to route'. The prompt 'Drag Draw from a pad'. On ship, a 25-word toast (qfn-play-23, -30). The board title appears on the card, the panel header and the world plate. Board 3's ask ('Use layer 2 and vias, and cool the exposed pad', station.ts via logic.ts:93) and the step text 'layer 2, vias, thermal pad' (station.ts:73) both tell the method, not the goal. For a new player the panel competes with the board, which should be the whole interface.
findings.fix: Card step text: 'Lay out board 1/2/3' only. Panel: drop the header (the plate in the world names the board) and the ask paragraph. Keep the net chips and a single 'Grade now' row; move Loop, Chip and Track rows to icons on the board (the loop glow already exists, the chip glow already exists, and par can show as a small 'cost / par' meter on the jig). Ask lines: 'J1 has to reach a cable' / 'Each supply pair needs its own cap' / 'VIN and GND have to cross', with no method words. Ship toast: show the 'teach' line on its own for 4 s on the shipped board before the next board loads (see the dropIn finding).
findings.verify: Word count of the bench shot (qfn-play-14 retake) is 25 or fewer outside the board. The board name appears once.
findings.verify_reason: qfn-play-14 and verify-qfn-play-10 show the board name three times: the card ('Board 1 · Sensor breakout'), the panel ('BOARD 1/3 … Sensor breakout') and the world plate ('BOARD 1 · SENSOR BREAKOUT'). That breaks DR-41. Card, panel, plate, legend and prompt come to about 60 words, and the ship toast in qfn-play-30 adds 25 more. The board 3 ask (logic.ts:93) and step text (station.ts:73) describe the method ('Use layer 2 and vias'), which DR-39 forbids.
findings.fix_correction: Keep one short constraint line in the panel or on the jig, e.g. 'One layer: tracks can't cross'. That's the rule the puzzle teaches (AGENTS 10), not method text, so don't drop the ask completely.

findings.title: Bench prompt says 'Drag · Draw from a pad' while the board's first task is placement, and keeps saying it mid-drag
findings.problem: prompt() returns {Drag, 'Draw from a pad'} whenever any net is unjoined (station.ts:432). Each board starts with scrambled parts and a connector facing the wrong way: board 1's J1 at (10,1) rot 1 fails 'mouth out', and the ask says 'Place J1, R1 and C1'. Yet the only instruction line tells the player to draw first. Drawing first leads into dead ends on a one-layer board, because 'placement comes before routing' is the very lesson (logic.ts:80). While a part is being dragged by its body the prompt still reads 'Draw from a pad' (qfn-play-53). On board 3 the prompt never mentions vias or the thermal pad, even though the chip shows 135 °C.
findings.fix: Order prompt() as follows. drag → {Drag,'Drop it on the board'}. Placement problems in the live report (mouth or off-board) → {Drag,'Move J1 to an edge, mouth out'}. Any part never moved yet on a fresh board → {Drag,'Slide the parts into place'}. Then the net, check, thermal ({V,'Cool the chip'} when thermal.temp>limit and the nets are done) and ship cases.
findings.verify: Start-of-board bench shot shows the placement prompt. A mid-drag screenshot shows 'Drop it on the board'.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced. At board start the live problems list opens with 'J1 must sit on a board edge with its mouth facing out', yet the prompt reads 'Drag · Draw from a pad'. In the middle of a body drag of C1 (drag={id:C1}) the prompt still reads 'Draw from a pad' (verify-qfn-play-11). prompt() has no drag or placement branch (station.ts:428-434).

findings.title: Moving a resistor or capacitor by its big coloured ends draws a track instead; the grab body is a 0.1 m sliver
findings.problem: The two-pin parts are drawn as two large coloured end caps, which are the pads (userData.pad, station.ts:173), with a 0.1 m body between them. Pressing a pad starts a stroke (station.ts:331-332). Only the body starts a move (bodyAt, :308-313). At the bench camera the body is about 30 px and the caps are the most visible, colourful thing on the part. In s4 a natural 'grab C1 by its end and drag it toward the chip' drew a 3-cell VDD track toward the chip (qfn-play-50, -51) and raised the toast 'No top-layer copper under the QFN body', which a new player won't connect to what they meant to do. Turning a part by clicking it again is also undiscoverable: the prompt says so only while hovering a selected body.
findings.fix: Make the move handle clearly the biggest grip. Raise the body to 0.13×0.09×0.12 with an ink grip ridge, and shrink the caps to 0.035 wide. Add a rule in pointer(): a press on a pad of a part that has no copper attached yet, followed by a drag whose first step leaves the part's footprint in the direction away from its other pad, moves the part instead (scrambled parts are always unrouted at the start). Also show a small rotate-arrow decal on the selected part's body for 'click to turn'.
findings.verify: Repeat s4 step 1. Dragging C1 from (10,7) moves it, and design.traces stays empty. A spec asserts a drag that starts on an unrouted pad moves the part.
findings.verify_reason: Pressing a pad starts a stroke, not a move (station.ts:310, 331-332). My drag starting on C1's end pad began a stroke and raised the short toast, and C1 stayed at (10,7). The size claim is overstated. The body is 0.10 m wide and each cap 0.045 m (station.ts:173), so the body isn't a sliver. But the two colourful caps sit over the pad cells, and the caps plus the flat pads make up most of the part's clickable area.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-qfn-play/v2-bench.mjs log 'after pad drag C1': place unchanged, short toast
findings.fix_correction: Don't use the 'press on an unrouted pad, drag away from the other pad = move' rule. Dragging outward from a pad is the normal way to start a track, so this would break routing. The proposed sizes also collide: a 0.13 m body reaches ±0.065 and would overlap caps 0.035 wide at ±0.072. Instead, make the caps low and flat so they read as copper pads (≤0.02 m tall). Make the body the tall grip (0.12 wide, caps moved to ±0.09). Add press-and-hold (≥0.3 s without moving) anywhere on a part to move it.

findings.title: The bench session is far longer than other rooms (about 40 inputs, 720 s limit), so room lengths are uneven
findings.problem: The clean solve in tests/station-qfn.spec.ts and s2 is 10 part moves, 17 track strokes, 5 vias, 1 layer switch, 3 checks and 3 ships, plus a crate run. The reference board-3 route alone is 8 tracks and 5 vias (logic.ts:314-317), all at par with no slack. The station's own time limit is 720 s (station.ts:51), six times the 120 s cable-floor default (src/sim/grade.ts:3). A first-time player needs several CHECK/undo cycles per board, so a realistic clean solve is 6–12 minutes, more than twice the median room. It is also one unbroken stretch at one camera, with no walking or physical break between boards. The three boards are fun individually (see notes), but three in a row with escalating rules is a long, quiet stretch for a slapstick game. Manual-mode time can't measure bench seconds (s2 reports 9.25 s), so this needs a human timing.
findings.fix: Break the session up with the room: after each SHIP the player stands up to carry the board to the oven (see the room-backdrop finding), which gives a 15–20 s physical break and a juicy moment per board. Give board 3 one slack cell of par (42→44) so 'elegant' needs understanding rather than exact replication. Measure real bench time with 3 playtesters (NEXT_STEPS §3) and set limits.time to the median clean time ×1.3.
findings.verify: Human timing of a fresh player: clean solve ≤ 2× the median clean solve across rooms (DR-08). Spec timing with the oven leg added.
findings.verify_reason: The input count is right for the reference solve (logic.ts:309-317), and limits.time is 720 (station.ts:51). The comparison is skewed, though. The other station rooms set 360–540 s (arcade 480, garage 420, observatory 360, spectrum 540), so 720 is 1.3–2× its peers, not 6×, and 120 s is a cable-floor default. Real bench time hasn't been measured (manual mode can't show it), so the DR-08 breach is unproven. P2 until a human timing exists.

findings.title: About 1197 draw calls at the start camera (review 3 measured 850), far over the 250 budget
findings.problem: snap().drawCalls = 1197 at the start shot and 1193 in the survey (s1 log). Review 3 (REVIEW_B perf table) recorded 850 for qfn, so the clutter pass (max:220, src/levels/qfn.ts:24) made it worse. The game reaches 60 fps on the host GPU in manual mode, but integrated and phone GPUs will drop frames, and src/game.ts adaptQuality will cut the effects the toon look depends on. Every clutter prop is its own set of toon and outline meshes. The board, pucks and labels add dozens more.
findings.fix: Instance repeated clutter kinds (box, cabinet, chair, bin, cone) with InstancedMesh per kind and colour. Bodies stay in Rapier, and the instance matrices update only for awake bodies. Merge static decor per material in room.ts: shelf bins, the minis, the reel bank and posters are already in decorRoot and freeze() could merge them by material. Cap QFN clutter at max:150 until instancing lands.
findings.verify: s1-start log: drawCalls ≤ 250 at the start camera and in the survey.

findings.fix_correction: Before instancing, check that the outline pass supports InstancedMesh. Otherwise instanced clutter loses its ink outlines, which are a hard toon rule. A quick first step is turning off outlines on tiny clutter (paper, mugs) and capping max at 150.

findings.title: The ratsnest draws dashed lines to invisible parts before the crate arrives, and doesn't follow a part being dragged
findings.problem: Before partsReady, syncParts hides every part except U1 (station.ts:183), but redraw() still builds the ratsnest from design.place. Dashed lines run from U1's pads to empty board cells (qfn-play-40), which looks broken. During a body drag, ghost() moves the part mesh to drag.to (station.ts:360), but the ratsnest and the pad rings are computed from the committed placement (station.ts:201), so the dashes keep pointing at the empty cell the part left (qfn-play-53). The live feedback that tells a player 'this placement shortens the route' is exactly what placement depends on, and it's missing while dragging.
findings.fix: In redraw(), when !partsReady, skip the ratsnest and the legend. During a drag, compute it with `ratsnest(b,{...d,place:{...d.place,[drag.id]:{at:drag.to,rot:d.place[drag.id].rot}}})` so the dashes stretch live as the part moves. Rate-limit it to cell changes, which ghost() already does.
findings.verify: Retake qfn-play-40 (no dashes) and qfn-play-53 (the dashes end at C1's ghost position).
findings.verify_reason: Both halves reproduced. Before the crate arrives, dashed lines run from U1 to empty cells (verify-qfn-play-02). During a body drag, C1's ghost sits near (3,5) while the red and blue dashes still end at its old cell (verify-qfn-play-11). redraw() uses the committed design.place (station.ts:201), and ghost() only moves the mesh (station.ts:360).

Parse problems[0] for a part id, flash that part's selection frame red, and pulse the chevron on a connector-mouth problem. Draw net rings only for connectivity problems. Rings pulse on every pad of every unjoined net, while the cause named is J1's mouth, and J1 gets no distinct cue (verify-qfn-play-12). findings.title: Board 3's chip glows 135 °C hot before anything is wired or powered, washing out its pin labels
findings.problem: update() tints the QFN body and pulses its heat sprite from live.thermal whenever the board has a thermal pad (station.ts:394-396). The temperature model is chipTemp(vias) only (logic.ts:233, :276-278). The moment board 3 loads, with no VIN track and nothing plugged into J1, the chip glows red-orange 'over limit' (qfn-play-30) and the panel reads 'Chip 135 °C'. That teaches the wrong cause (heat with no power) and makes the first thing the player sees an unexplained alarm. The glow also covers the chip's VIN and ISET pin tags.
findings.fix: Show heat only once the chip is powered in the model: VIN and GND nets joined, or after a CHECK (the 'power-on test'). Before that, show the chip neutral with a small thermometer icon reading '?'. Keep glow opacity ≤0.35 and raise the sprite to y 0.3 so the pin tags stay readable.
findings.verify: Board 3 start shot: no glow. After VIN and GND are routed with no vias, the glow appears. After 5 vias it's cool.
findings.verify_reason: At board 3 load, thermal={vias:0,temp:135,limit:70} with no net joined (VIN 1/4, GND 1/6). The chip body glows red-orange, and the VIN and ISET tags are washed out (verify-qfn-play-17). chipTemp depends only on vias (logic.ts:233), which shows heat with no power. That's a truthfulness slip at the level taught.

findings.title: New-board parts drop from 0.6–0.9 m and look like they're floating over the room; the ship toast describes the board that just left

findings.title: Decoupling 'current bursts' read as five static white blobs, and the loop glow is barely visible
findings.problem: After CHECK, drawLoops() spawns five 0.024 m beads per loop spaced u = -k×0.09 (station.ts:230). On board 1's 4-cell loop they bunch at C1 as overlapping white balls wider than the track (crop qfn-play-24). The additive loop glow (opacity 0.55, #7dffb0×1.4) washes out to near-white on the red and blue copper, so the green 'short enough' meaning doesn't read. This is the room's main visual for decoupling (review 4 asked for it), and it doesn't land. It also shows moving dots on a board with no power source (DR-29).
findings.fix: Bead radius 0.014, spacing -k×0.2, speed so one lap takes 0.6 s on a 4-cell loop. Draw the loop as an ink-outlined ribbon (#2fd47a for OK, #ff8a3d for too long) 0.02 m above the copper rather than an additive overlay. Run the bursts only after the board is 'powered' by the CHECK power-on test, with a tiny plug icon on J1, so the dots mean current.

findings.verify_reason: In the crop after CHECK (verify-qfn-play-14) the beads are overlapping white balls bunched at C1, wider than the track, and the additive glow turns the loop copper nearly white. The green 'OK' meaning doesn't read (station.ts:223, 230).

findings.title: Station toast follows Pip into the room after standing up
findings.problem: After Esc, the last bench toast ('U1 is fixed: the QFN is the anchor everything else fits around.') stays over the room view with the walking prompt (qfn-play-57). setActive(false) (station.ts:377) doesn't hide the toast, and it only expires on toastUntil while game.running. The arcade fixed the same thing (R3B N2) by hiding the toast in setActive.
findings.fix: In setActive(false): if(this.toast)this.toast.hidden=true. Also hide the station panel while walking, which shows 'BOARD 1/3 · ONE LAYER Sensor breakout' over the room even at spawn (qfn-play-01; on a phone it covers the middle of the screen, qfn-play-60).

The panel 'BOARD 1/3 · ONE LAYER Sensor breakout' also shows while walking from spawn (v1 log 'start').

notes.fun: What works: the bench puzzle is fun. It plays like Flow Free with real stakes. Dragging a track cell by cell with rising ticks, the bell when a pad of the same net is reached, and the 'VDD is joined' chime are satisfying. Par turns each board into a small optimisation puzzle, and CHECK is free, so experimenting doesn't cost grades, unlike the arcade. Board 3 escalates nicely (the crossing that becomes possible with a via, the chip cooling as thermal vias go in). The crate pickup gives a ring burst and a satisfying clunk. What's missing: the room part lasts about 5 s (crate at t≈1 s, bench at t≈5 s). After that 120 props, the pick-and-place, the oven and the AOI are only scenery, with no cable, no chaos route and no physical bonus. The one natural chaos act (throwing the crate at the bench) is ignored and counted as damage. The success beats are flat: the next board appears in the same frame and the finished board becomes a slab on the side table. The win push-in frames Pip cut off at the bottom-left corner behind the result card (qfn-play-36). Throwing the crate at a coworker does trigger the '!' bubble (qfn-play-90), so the slapstick systems work in this room. They're just never invited.
notes.playability: The clean route is short and clear: spawn → crate (2.3 m) → bench (about 10 m), all in a clutter lane, with no dead walking (the longest leg is about 2 s). The crate never wedged in five throw tests (pnp, aoi, rack gap, side table, over the bench): it always landed at floor or tabletop height and stayed reachable, because job items win grab priority within reach. Problems: (1) P0 on a phone: CHECK, SHIP, TURN, LAYER and VIA are off-screen and have only keyboard fallbacks, so the job can't be finished on touch. (2) The prompt 'Set the crate on the bench' shows in places where E drops the crate on the floor. (3) A cabinet+box clutter stack in front of the bench hides Pip at the default camera. (4) Moving a two-pin part by its big coloured ends draws a track. The grab body is a 30 px sliver. (5) There are 1197 draw calls at the start camera. (6) Room damage and bench mistakes share limits.damage=1. Modeless input itself (drag body to move, click again to turn, drag from a pad to draw, tap a track to cut, V mid-stroke) works through the real pointer and is a big improvement on review 4's nine modal tools. Undo and the refusal toasts ('C1 would sit on U1', 'short') make mistakes cheap.
notes.clarity: The room reads well. The yellow taped spot, the STOCK sign and the marker lead to the crate, and the bench is mid-room under its own light. At the bench the board is well framed at 16:10 and the net colours match the chips in the panel, but the HUD around it is heavy: about 60–80 words, and the board name three times (card, panel header, world plate). The prompt says 'Draw from a pad' while the real first task is placement. Pin tags and key letters are 5–10 px. The ratsnest dangles to invisible parts before the crate arrives and doesn't follow a dragged part. Job yellow is spent on a cart, a chair, splitters and 'locked' connector caps (which mean the opposite of 'grab me'). The marker floats 1.5 m above the crate and lands on Pip's hat at the bench step. Board 3's chip glows 'over temperature' before anything is wired. The send-back toast states the cause ('J1 must sit on a board edge with its mouth facing out'), but red rings cover every pad, not J1. Could a new player solve it from the scene alone? Board 1's 'mouth out' rule and board 2's 'cap hugs its pins' rule need the panel sentence or a failed check first. Board 3's 'start a layer-2 track on a via' is still only discovered through a refusal toast.
notes.teaching: (Not my primary dimension.) Placement-before-routing and one-layer-can't-cross are learned by doing. Decoupling is measured on real copper paths, and thermal vias in parallel use an honest formula. But the chip's heat shows with no power, and the loop beads look like current on an unpowered board (DR-29/30 territory for the teach reviewer).
notes.models: (Not my primary dimension.) Bench pucks are chunky and readable, and the QFN body is a clean ink tile. Shipped boards on the side table are flat slabs with no detail. The parts crate is a plain prop box tinted yellow, with no job-item stripes or icon.
